q8.answer: The MERGE matches on order_id and updates a stored row only when the staged winner beats it: a later updated_at, with ties going to the larger row hash. Stage keeps one winner per order_id before the MERGE, so duplicates from the lookback overlap or a re-run collapse to one candidate, and an older copy that loses that comparison leaves the stored newer row alone.

q9.answer: The high-water mark is the single row in etl_watermark, and its value is the 02:00 UTC cutoff of the nightly run. It is written inside the commit transaction, together with the MERGE and the success row, and only when the cutoff is later than the stored value, so it moves forward only and never on a failed attempt.

q10.answer: The MERGE into orders, the hwm update and the success row commit in one warehouse transaction, so dashboards see either the previous night's orders or the fully merged new night, never a partial merge. Dashboards read only orders, and a failure rolls the whole transaction back, leaving orders and the hwm unchanged; if no commit has happened by 06:00 they show the last good night and the staleness alert fires.

q11.answer: Each attempt deletes its run_id's rows from orders_stage at step 4 before loading, so a retry under the same run_id clears whatever the failed attempt staged and cannot double rows. The retry re-reads the hwm; since the failed attempt committed nothing, the hwm is unchanged and the retry extracts the same window (hwm minus 2 hours up to the fixed 02:00 cutoff) as the first attempt.

q12.answer: A reload ignores the updated_at window and re-reads every row of that order-creation day from the replica, stages it under its own new run_id (so it never touches the nightly run's staging rows), picks winners, and applies the same guarded MERGE, so a newer replica version replaces a stale stored row while a row already current is left alone. A reload never changes the hwm, because its run kind is reload and the hwm update in step 6 applies only to nightly runs.
